record.title: New Zealand's Strategy for Artificial Intelligence: Investing with confidence (Accelerating Private Sector AI Adoption and Innovation)
record.summary: New Zealand's first AI strategy, deliberately focused on practical adoption of AI by businesses rather than high-end development. It takes a light-touch, principles-based approach: existing frameworks such as privacy, consumer protection and human rights law apply and are to be updated as new risks arise, with no regulatory overlay beyond existing law. It confirms New Zealand's adoption of the OECD AI Principles, including robustness, security and safety and accountability, points businesses to the companion Responsible AI Guidance for Businesses, and commits to work in global AI governance fora, including on protecting people from harmful or negligent AI use.
record.notes: Published in July 2025 by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, with a foreword by Shane Reti, Minister of Science, Innovation and Technology, together with the companion Responsible AI Guidance for Businesses (NZ-03). It complements the work on AI in the public sector led by the Minister for Digitising Government. MBIE states that it used AI to develop aspects of the strategy.

verification.note: Recheck of 17 Oct 2026: every stored copy of the MBIE strategy page (11 and 17 Oct 2026, also with the browser retry) is a JavaScript bot-check page of the site's web application firewall (Incapsula), and so are MBIE's news release and the Cabinet minute requested in this run. The strategy itself was stored in this run as a 22-page PDF from mbie.govt.nz; it confirms the title, July 2025, MBIE as publisher, the minister's foreword, the light-touch and principles-based approach, the OECD AI Principles, the companion business guidance and the international commitments. Version 1's notes said the web page did not explicitly state the existing-laws approach (the PDF states it) and showed 'Last updated: 22 October 2025', a web page stamp.

title.quote: New Zealand’s Strategy for Artificial Intelligence: Investing with confidence JULY 2025 Accelerating Private Sector AI Adoption and Innovation

issuing_body.quote: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
As a companion document to this Strategy, the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment has published Responsible AI Guidance for Businesses.

status.quote: This document is a guide only. It should not be used as a substitute for legislation or legal advice.

legal_force.quote: This document is a guide only. It should not be used as a substitute for legislation or legal advice.

summary.quote: Until now, New Zealand was the only OECD country that had not published an AI strategy
the strategic approach we have taken is deliberately focused on practical adoption rather than high-end development.
New Zealand is taking a light-touch and principles-based approach to AI policy.
New Zealand has existing regulatory frameworks (e.g., privacy, consumer protection, human rights) which are largely principles-based and technology-neutral.
These frameworks can be updated as and when needed to enable AI innovation, and to address new risks and unintended interactions with legislation.
The adoption of these principles does not require additional regulatory overlay beyond existing law.
New Zealand will continue to engage in the most important global fora on AI governance to influence the responsible development of AI
improving global security, or protecting people from harmful or negligent AI use

notes.quote: Hon Dr Shane Reti, Minister of Science, Innovation & Technology
This strategy complements the work being undertaken by Hon Judith Collins KC, Minister for Digitising Government, who is driving adoption of AI within the public sector.
MBIE has used AI to develop aspects of this Strategy

judgment.status_reasoning: A non-binding strategy published in July 2025 ('a guide only', not a substitute for legislation). Nothing stored shows it replaced or withdrawn; 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: A national AI strategy whose main focus is adoption, with limited safety content (OECD principles, the approach to new risks); the published scope_note stays and is supported by the text ('light-touch', no AI-specific regulation beyond existing law).
judgment.date_reasoning: The PDF gives only 'JULY 2025', so date_published stays 2025-07.

open_questions: MBIE's news release and the Cabinet minute of decision could not be stored (bot-check pages); the day of publication is not shown by any stored file, so the date stays at month precision.
